passages.title: Promising Early Results
passages.text: Although the proposal appears practical, its success depends on assumptions that have not yet been tested. We should therefore distinguish between promising early results and evidence of lasting improvement.
passages.levelRationale: The argument qualifies an initial judgment and distinguishes between related kinds of evidence.

passages.title: Interpreting Public Data
passages.text: Public data can reveal meaningful patterns, provided we remember that measurement choices shape the picture we see. A persuasive chart may clarify a trend, yet still conceal uncertainty or exclude relevant experience.
passages.levelRationale: The passage develops a qualified abstract claim about interpretation and hidden limitations.

passages.title: The Appearance of Efficiency
passages.text: A shorter meeting may appear more efficient, but speed alone is a poor measure of progress. If unresolved concerns merely resurface later, the saved time is largely an illusion.
passages.levelRationale: The passage challenges a superficial measure and develops its qualification through a hypothetical consequence.

passages.title: Travel and Restoration
passages.text: Travel is often presented as an escape from routine, though unfamiliar places can be demanding in their own way. Its restorative value may lie less in comfort than in renewed attention.
passages.levelRationale: An abstract reflection reframes a familiar idea through concession and precise comparison.
